prompt:
Our platform engineering team is trying to build an internal reference library of classical strategy principles that engineering leads can actually use when making real decisions — things like access control policy, service ownership boundaries, and when to reveal product roadmap details publicly.

I have a raw dump file at `drafts/unprocessed/raw_principles_dump.txt` with 5 entries from various sources. The problem is the source quality varies wildly — some are from proper historical texts, some are from the internet with no real backing, and some are somewhere in between. I need each one turned into a proper structured record.

Please produce a file called `principles_library.json` that contains all 5 entries in a consistent structured format. Each record needs to clearly separate the original classical idea from the historical context, from the modern interpretation, and must clearly indicate how reliable each entry is based on its source. The library will be used by engineers, so at least some entries should include concrete software/systems analogies.

The reliability assessment for each entry is critical — we cannot afford to present internet folklore with the same authority as properly sourced classical material.
